causal_chain: If gains disappear when coalition competition is removed under a matched control, the frontier mechanism is likely unnecessary.
If scoring also includes an explicit conflict term against non-selected coalitions, candidates that match one taste while contradicting another can be separated from broadly compatible items.

If the model decomposes each user's training history into a small set of learned latent coalitions, different candidate items can route to different coalitions instead of competing through one global preference vector.
This coalition-routing plus conflict suppression should improve ordering of ambiguous and multi-intent cases in full-sort ranking.
Users in ML-1M often have mixed tastes that are poorly summarized by a single embedding or uniform history pool.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any observed improvement may come only from increased parameter count and a history-attention encoder, not from coalition competition or the explicit conflict channel.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with a matched mechanism-off version that uses the same history encoder but only supportive aggregation, the frontier model should show larger gains for users with more diverse training histories than for users with short concentrated histories.
If coalition competition is the real driver, ablating only the conflict term should remove a substantial fraction of the frontier advantage while leaving parameter count nearly unchanged.

The frontier model should assign lower scores than the mechanism-off control to candidates that strongly align with one inferred taste coalition while conflicting with another coalition built from the same user history.
expected_evidence: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender can train under pairwise BPR-style input using only train-split user histories and full-sort evaluation.
A matched control with identical embedding sizes and history encoder but no coalition competition should narrow or erase gains if the proposed mechanism is not causal.
Full-sort NDCG@10 stratified by user history diversity should favor the frontier model more strongly in high-diversity strata than in low-diversity strata.
Inspection of routing weights should show candidate-specific concentration on different user coalitions rather than a nearly uniform reuse of the same pooled representation.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched mechanism-off control with the same embeddings, history encoder, and parameter budget matches or exceeds the frontier model on full-sort NDCG@10 overall and on high-diversity-user slices, then the coalition-competition hypothesis is falsified.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core user representation from a single vector or graph-smoothed vector into a candidate-routed set of latent history coalitions, adds a new support-versus-conflict interaction structure at scoring time, and requires custom executable capability for coalition construction and competitive routing that is not available in the current profile catalog.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that represents each user's training history as a small set of latent taste coalitions, then scores each candidate by routing to its most supportive coalition while subtracting conflict from rival coalitions, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over conventional single-channel collaborative filtering because it can preserve mixed preferences without collapsing them into one static compatibility signal.
implementation_requirements: Add logging for routing entropy and conflict magnitude to support falsification analysis.
Build user coalition memories from train-only interacted item embeddings via learned slot initialization and a small number of slot-attention refinement steps.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender in PyTorch.
Score a user-item pair with a support term from the best-matching coalition and a conflict penalty from non-selected coalitions.
Support full-sort inference over all items using cached coalition memories computed from the training history only.
Train with pairwise ranking loss under the frozen protocol.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same item/user embedding dimensions, same history-to-slot encoder backbone, same optimizer family, and same training loop, but remove coalition competition by replacing support-minus-conflict scoring with a single pooled supportive aggregation over the same encoded history.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace single-vector user preference scoring with candidate-conditioned routing over multiple learned history coalitions plus an explicit rival-coalition conflict penalty.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off keeps the same train-only history encoder and parameter budget but collapses the learned coalitions into one pooled history representation and removes the rival-coalition conflict subtraction, so candidates are scored only by supportive aggregation without coalition competition.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Implement a 3-slot coalition-memory recommender with support-minus-conflict scoring and compare it against a parameter-matched pooled-history control that uses the identical encoder but no coalition competition.
blind_projection.research_question: Does candidate-conditioned routing over multiple latent user taste coalitions, with explicit suppression from rival coalitions, improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 beyond what can be explained by a matched history-attention encoder alone?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with 3 coalition slots, shared embedding tables, and lightweight slot-attention refinement should fit within the stated qualification budget on ML-1M because memory construction is linear in observed train interactions and full-sort evaluation can reuse cached user coalition states.
